A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Matrix3D and provide readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Matrix3D experiments on pose estimation, novel view synthesis, depth prediction, and reconstruction, plus appendix ablations and training-progress analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative experiments and appendix analyses and presents additional qualitative reconstruction examples.

M1.justification: The multi-view encoder/decoder, modality representations, masked-learning procedure, v-prediction objective, and 3DGS reconstruction pipeline and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training datasets and evaluation tasks remain unchanged, including the appendix ETH3D and T&T evaluations. The new reconstruction illustrations fall within the object and indoor coverage already described in v1 Section 4.4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the pose, novel-view synthesis, depth, reconstruction, and appendix comparisons. The qualitative comparison formerly shown in Figure 7 is retained as v2 Figure 6.

E3.justification: Reported splits, metrics, view configurations, training budgets, and reconstruction procedures are unchanged. Moving normalization instructions to the appendix and clarifying 'diffusion samples' in Table 2's caption do not change the protocols.

E4.justification: The qualitative case study of reconstruction from three unposed images gains new object and indoor examples in v2 Figure 7; the earlier examples remain in appendix Figure 9. Multi-task ablations, training-progress analyses, and outdoor-depth tests are unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including Table 6's CLIP scores with the same plus/minus values. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test information is added.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 7 presents five additional qualitative reconstruction examples: three object scenes and two indoor scenes. All numerical table entries and Figure 8's training curves remain unchanged, including the appendix tables whose numbers switch between 9 and 10.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(2), the appendix accumulation-regularization formula, and the mathematical descriptions remain unchanged. No formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: v1 Section 5 claims state-of-the-art performance in every downstream task; v2 restricts this claim to pose estimation and novel view synthesis, excluding depth prediction. The abstract and central unified-model contribution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The depth-versus-point-cloud interpretation, explanations for depth-assisted predictions and ablation convergence, and outdoor-data limitation are retained. The limitations section moves from supplementary Section 9.5 to 10.5 without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing instructions, reconstruction settings, and access information are retained. Scene and camera normalization details move from Section 3.3 to supplementary Section 8 without changing their content.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 141 cited works and substantive research positioning. The related-work wording is lightly shortened, with no added or removed references or revised novelty relationship.

P1.justification: Several passages are shortened, normalization details move to the appendix, and a new acknowledgments section shifts supplementary section numbering. These are limited edits within the existing narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main reconstruction figure receives new panels and a revised label, while Figures 6 and 7 exchange identities through reordering. Table 6 and several appendix displays move, Figure 10 occupies a separate final page, and Table 2's caption clarifies 'diffusion samples'.

improvement.justification: The narrower conclusion better reflects the retained mixed depth and reconstruction results in Tables 4-6. New object and indoor reconstruction examples replace main-text panels duplicated in the appendix, adding useful qualitative support. These are limited gains; the method, quantitative evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
